walkthrough: Goal: ink a line that thins to a point at both ends without lifting into a second tool, shade with the pencil laid on its side, draw lines of one even width whatever the pressure, and paint with a plain hard round brush; every stroke looks the same after reopening.

Entry: open OpenPaint on the tablet (2880 x 1800, landscape) on an empty library; the pen draws with the Ink Pen. Tap the Brush button: the panel lists the brushes by job, each with a stroke it painted: Pencil, Ink Pen, Inker, Monoline, Hard Round, Soft Brush, then StreamLine.

Inker: tap Inker and draw a long line. While the pen is down the line grows from a fine point at its start to its full width; its end under the pen is blunt and full width (the stroke does not know yet where it ends). Lift the pen: in the next frame the last stretch narrows to a point too, so the finished line is thin at both ends and full width in between. The line left is exactly the one shown after the lift.
Undo takes the line away whole, redo brings it back exactly; the taper is part of the stroke, not a step of its own.
Leave the app and come back: the line is exactly as it was after the lift.

Pencil with tilt: tap the Brush button, tap Pencil. Draw a stroke holding the pen upright, then one beside it with the pen laid over (70 degrees from upright): the tilted one is wider and lighter, graphite on the paper's tooth like the side of a pencil lead; held as for writing (up to 60 degrees: the hand leans the pen about 45) the pencil draws as before.
Monoline: tap the Brush button, tap Monoline: its StreamLine reads 60 % at first. Draw a light line and a hard one: both are exactly one width (pressure changes nothing), smoothed by the StreamLine.
Hard Round: tap the Brush button, tap Hard Round. A light stroke is thin and faint, a hard one wide and solid; where a stroke crosses itself it never darkens (it covers, as the Ink Pen does).

Failure and cancel: a stroke the size of a dot stays a dot; a stroke shorter than both of the Inker's tapers is thin all along and never wider than its full width. A pen that reports no tilt draws the Pencil as before. Ink Pen and Soft Brush draw exactly as before, and every stroke drawn before this version keeps its look.
Reopen: leave and come back: every stroke is exactly as it was, and each brush still has its StreamLine.
